full_judgment:
K. Hossain, J.—In this Rule a question of law is involved and the facts are net in dispute. The undisputed facts are that the predecessor of the Sonali Bank which was the National Bank of Pakistan obtained a money decree against Kushtia Sugarcane Mills Limited on 24.8.67 for a sum of Rs. 13,278/19 and put the decree into execution on 20th February, 1968 in Money Execution Case. No. 52 of 1969 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Kushtia. On 30th March, 1968 the immovable properties of the judgment-debtor company were attached and the notice under Order 21 rule 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued and Served on 30th of April, 1968 on which date the court also directed the properties so attached to be put to auction sale fixing the date of sale on 24th June, 1968. Before the tale could take place on 2nd June, 1968 an order was passed by the Vice-Chairman of the then East Pakistan. 

 3. Mr. Saadat Ali Khan, the learned Advocate, has appeared on behalf of the Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property Management Board, Bangladesh and has submitted that the true construction of the article is that the moment the property becomes attachment, seizure or sale in execution of a Civil Court decree. 

 "5. All enemy property vesting in the Custodian shall be exempt from attachment, seizure or sale in execution of a civil court decree or orders of any other authority." 

 5. A plain reading of the article shows that all enemy properties which have vested in the Custodian shall in exempt from attachment, seizure or sale n execution of a Civil Court decree. The question is when the property vests in the Custodian? Mr. Asrarul Hossain has referred to Rule 182(b) of Defence of Pakistan Rules and the rule provides that the Central Government may appoint a Custodian for Pakistan and one or more Deputy Custodians or Assistant Custodians of Enemy Property for such local areas as may be prescribed and may by order vest or provide for and regulate the vesting, in the prescribed custodian such enemy properly as may be prescribed. 

 7. Turning to the Article under interpretation, we find that with the vesting in the Custodian, the property becomes immune from attachment, seizure or sale in execution of a civil court decree. What was the position on 2nd June, 1968 when the vesting order look effect? The property was already under attachment by an order of the civil court of 30th March, 1968. On true construction of the article all further proceedings, in our opinion, specially the sale in terms of this article could not take place. But for that matter the attachment did not become invalid or illegal. Mr. Hossain rightly submits that the court ought to have stayed further proceedings instead of dissolving the attachment. We find substance in his contention.
